subject: ACME commercial clearing — pricing, min-commit, invoicing & tax routing
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME order form — commercial & tax handoff

Team — attaching the redlined OF (v3) and the proposed pricing schedule. ACME is ready to move but we need sign-off from Legal + Finance on a few items before we send back: 

1) Minimum commit language
   - ACME asked to soften the stair-step language and cap penalties in year 1. Want to confirm what concessions we can make (limit to one-time true-up, not recurring).

2) Net terms / invoicing cadence
   - Procurement is asking for Net45. Finance: do we have an internal policy that disallows Net45 without credit review? If so, can we offer Net45 conditioned on approved credit check + initial deposit invoice?

3) Tax & invoicing entity
   - ACME provided two legal entities. They prefer invoices to go to ACME Instruments, Inc. (US) and have asked Redwood to confirm buyer bears taxes. Legal: we need explicit language on tax liability and any reverse-charge evidence required for EU customers (not relevant here, but flaggable). Finance: what evidence do we need from ACME to avoid withholding?

4) Attachment items
   - ACME_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (attached) — their markups in red
   - PricingSchedule_v2.xlsx (attached) — minor SKU mapping changes

Ask: Kimberly, please provide redline guidance on the proposed tax clause and the minimum-commit compromise (one-time true-up vs. recurring). Laura, pls confirm whether Net45 is permissible as an exception and list required documents (PO, tax cert). Ben, I’ll coordinate with the AE on next steps.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf, PricingSchedule_v2.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME order form — commercial & tax handoff

On Tue, Aug 15, 2028 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — attaching the redlined OF (v3) and the proposed pricing schedule. ACME is ready to move but we need sign-off from Legal + Finance on a few items before we send back:
>
> 1) Minimum commit language
> 2) Net terms / invoicing cadence
> 3) Tax & invoicing entity
> 4) Attachment items

Thanks Jordan — reviewed quickly and added inline notes to the attached redline. High-level legal stance below: 

- Minimum commit: We can accept a softened stair-step for year 1 if the order form includes a single true-up clause (net difference payable within 30 days of true-up), and we retain our right to terminate for non-payment. We should avoid language that converts true-ups into ongoing recurring credits.

- Net terms: Standard is Net30. We will not unilaterally extend to Net45 without credit/AR approval. If Sales wants to pursue Net45, put condition: "Net45 to be effective only after completion of credit review and execution of payment addendum."

- Tax allocation: Add explicit tax clause: "Buyer is responsible for all sales, use, VAT/GST, and other transaction-based taxes, except for taxes imposed on Redwood's net income." Also add a sentence allowing Redwood to request tax residency documents where applicable. For US invoicing, if ACME requests invoice to a different entity than the contracting entity, include requirement for a signed PO referencing the entity.

- Invoicing entity: If Finance prefers invoicing to a Redwood US entity, legal is fine as long as PO and remit instructions are consistent.

I attached a short excerpt redline (ACME_OrderForm_legal_snippet.pdf) with the proposed tax sentence and payment-addendum placeholder.

Next steps: Laura — confirm what Finance needs (PO, tax cert, credit application) so we can get this back to ACME with a clean list. Once we have those items, I can prepare the final redline for the OF.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_legal_snippet.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Aug 2028 10:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME order form — commercial & tax handoff

Kimberly / Jordan — finance confirm below.

1) Net terms: We can support Net45 on a deal-by-deal basis but require the following before final terms are posted:
   - Completed credit application and approval by AR
   - Signed PO matching invoicing entity
   - Initial deposit invoice for 25% of the first-year commit issued on contract execution (to reduce credit exposure)

2) Tax documentation: For US customers, we need a signed Purchase Order and (if applicable) a resale certificate or IRS W-9 for entity verification. If ACME is paying from a non-US entity and requests no withholding, we’ll need a tax residency certificate or W-8BEN-E equivalent and legal confirmation on reverse-charge handling.

3) Invoicing entity: Finance prefers invoices issued to the legal contracting entity on the MSA. If ACME requests a different remit-to, we will accept a signed PO that explicitly references the billing entity.

4) Attachments: attached is our standard Invoice_Template_NET45.docx and a short checklist (PO + tax docs + credit app).

Once they return the PO + tax docs, AR will kick off the credit review (typically 3–5 business days). If Jordan / Ben want to accept Net45 earlier, we need RVP approval and to note that marketing credits / concessions should not be given for the payment term extension.

Laura Bennett
Finance - Accounts Receivable | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: Invoice_Template_NET45.docx, AR_Credit_Checklist.pdf

From: Sarah Ellis <sarah@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME order form — commercial & tax handoff

Jordan — thanks for the summary and to Kimberly / Laura for the quick review. A few items from our side: 

• We can provide a signed PO referencing ACME Instruments, Inc. (US) and can upload a US tax residency / W-9.
• We are comfortable with a 25% deposit at contract execution.
• Regarding taxes: ACME expects buyer to bear transaction taxes — we will accept the proposed tax clause language if Redwood can confirm invoicing to ACME Instruments, Inc. (US) and that Redwood will not require additional entity-level evidence beyond the PO + W-9 for US billing.

Request: Please include a one-sentence line in the order form near the tax section: "Buyer shall be responsible for all transaction-based taxes payable in connection with fees set forth herein." If you can return an updated OF with that line and the payment-addendum placeholder, we can route for signature. Also send the DocuSign link when ready.

Thanks — we want to close before the end of the month.

Best,
Sarah Ellis
Sr. Procurement Manager | ACME Instruments
sarah@acmecorp.com

Attachments: PO_ACME_000874.pdf (pending signature)
